blocks.source: Canto XXXIII
blocks.translation: Canto XXXIII

blocks.source: La bocca sollevò dal fiero pasto
blocks.translation: His mouth uplifted from his grim repast,

blocks.source: quel peccator, forbendola a’ capelli
blocks.translation: That sinner, wiping it upon the hair

blocks.source: del capo ch’elli avea di retro guasto.
blocks.translation: Of the same head that he behind had wasted.

blocks.source: Poi cominciò: «Tu vuo’ ch’io rinovelli
blocks.translation: Then he began: “Thou wilt that I renew

blocks.source: disperato dolor che ’l cor mi preme
blocks.translation: The desperate grief, which wrings my heart already

blocks.source: già pur pensando, pria ch’io ne favelli.
blocks.translation: To think of only, ere I speak of it;

blocks.source: Ma se le mie parole esser dien seme
blocks.translation: But if my words be seed that may bear fruit

blocks.source: che frutti infamia al traditor ch’i’ rodo,
blocks.translation: Of infamy to the traitor whom I gnaw,

blocks.source: parlar e lagrimar vedrai insieme.
blocks.translation: Speaking and weeping shalt thou see together.

blocks.source: Io non so chi tu se’ né per che modo
blocks.translation: I know not who thou art, nor by what mode

blocks.source: venuto se’ qua giù; ma fiorentino
blocks.translation: Thou hast come down here; but a Florentine

blocks.source: mi sembri veramente quand’ io t’odo.
blocks.translation: Thou seemest to me truly, when I hear thee.

blocks.source: Tu dei saper ch’i’ fui conte Ugolino,
blocks.translation: Thou hast to know I was Count Ugolino,

blocks.source: e questi è l’arcivescovo Ruggieri:
blocks.translation: And this one was Ruggieri the Archbishop;

blocks.source: or ti dirò perché i son tal vicino.
blocks.translation: Now I will tell thee why I am such a neighbour.

blocks.source: Che per l’effetto de’ suo’ mai pensieri,
blocks.translation: That, by effect of his malicious thoughts,

blocks.source: fidandomi di lui, io fossi preso
blocks.translation: Trusting in him I was made prisoner,

blocks.source: e poscia morto, dir non è mestieri;
blocks.translation: And after put to death, I need not say;

blocks.source: però quel che non puoi avere inteso,
blocks.translation: But ne’ertheless what thou canst not have heard,

blocks.source: cioè come la morte mia fu cruda,
blocks.translation: That is to say, how cruel was my death,

blocks.source: udirai, e saprai s’e’ m’ha offeso.
blocks.translation: Hear shalt thou, and shalt know if he has wronged me.

blocks.source: Breve pertugio dentro da la Muda,
blocks.translation: A narrow perforation in the mew,

blocks.source: la qual per me ha ’l titol de la fame,
blocks.translation: Which bears because of me the title of Famine,

blocks.source: e che conviene ancor ch’altrui si chiuda,
blocks.translation: And in which others still must be locked up,

blocks.source: m’avea mostrato per lo suo forame
blocks.translation: Had shown me through its opening many moons

blocks.source: più lune già, quand’ io feci ’l mal sonno
blocks.translation: Already, when I dreamed the evil dream

blocks.source: che del futuro mi squarciò ’l velame.
blocks.translation: Which of the future rent for me the veil.

blocks.source: Questi pareva a me maestro e donno,
blocks.translation: This one appeared to me as lord and master,

blocks.source: cacciando il lupo e ’ lupicini al monte
blocks.translation: Hunting the wolf and whelps upon the mountain

blocks.source: per che i Pisan veder Lucca non ponno.
blocks.translation: For which the Pisans cannot Lucca see.

blocks.source: Con cagne magre, studïose e conte
blocks.translation: With sleuth-hounds gaunt, and eager, and well trained,

blocks.source: Gualandi con Sismondi e con Lanfranchi
blocks.translation: Gualandi with Sismondi and Lanfranchi

blocks.source: s’avea messi dinanzi da la fronte.
blocks.translation: He had sent out before him to the front.

blocks.source: In picciol corso mi parieno stanchi
blocks.translation: After brief course seemed unto me forespent

blocks.source: lo padre e ’ figli, e con l’agute scane
blocks.translation: The father and the sons, and with sharp tushes

blocks.source: mi parea lor veder fender li fianchi.
blocks.translation: It seemed to me I saw their flanks ripped open.

blocks.source: Quando fui desto innanzi la dimane,
blocks.translation: When I before the morrow was awake,

blocks.source: pianger senti’ fra ’l sonno i miei figliuoli
blocks.translation: Moaning amid their sleep I heard my sons

blocks.source: ch’eran con meco, e dimandar del pane.
blocks.translation: Who with me were, and asking after bread.

blocks.source: Ben se’ crudel, se tu già non ti duoli
blocks.translation: Cruel indeed art thou, if yet thou grieve not,

blocks.source: pensando ciò che ’l mio cor s’annunziava;
blocks.translation: Thinking of what my heart foreboded me,

blocks.source: e se non piangi, di che pianger suoli?
blocks.translation: And weep’st thou not, what art thou wont to weep at?

blocks.source: Già eran desti, e l’ora s’appressava
blocks.translation: They were awake now, and the hour drew nigh

blocks.source: che ’l cibo ne solëa essere addotto,
blocks.translation: At which our food used to be brought to us,

blocks.source: e per suo sogno ciascun dubitava;
blocks.translation: And through his dream was each one apprehensive;

blocks.source: e io senti’ chiavar l’uscio di sotto
blocks.translation: And I heard locking up the under door

blocks.source: a l’orribile torre; ond’ io guardai
blocks.translation: Of the horrible tower; whereat without a word

blocks.source: nel viso a’ mie’ figliuoi sanza far motto.
blocks.translation: I gazed into the faces of my sons.

blocks.source: Io non piangëa, sì dentro impetrai:
blocks.translation: I wept not, I within so turned to stone;

blocks.source: piangevan elli; e Anselmuccio mio
blocks.translation: They wept; and darling little Anselm mine

blocks.source: disse: “Tu guardi sì, padre! che hai?”.
blocks.translation: Said: ‘Thou dost gaze so, father, what doth ail thee?’

blocks.source: Perciò non lagrimai né rispuos’ io
blocks.translation: Still not a tear I shed, nor answer made

blocks.source: tutto quel giorno né la notte appresso,
blocks.translation: All of that day, nor yet the night thereafter,

blocks.source: infin che l’altro sol nel mondo uscìo.
blocks.translation: Until another sun rose on the world.

blocks.source: Come un poco di raggio si fu messo
blocks.translation: As now a little glimmer made its way

blocks.source: nel doloroso carcere, e io scorsi
blocks.translation: Into the dolorous prison, and I saw

blocks.source: per quattro visi il mio aspetto stesso,
blocks.translation: Upon four faces my own very aspect,

blocks.source: ambo le man per lo dolor mi morsi;
blocks.translation: Both of my hands in agony I bit;

blocks.source: ed ei, pensando ch’io ’l fessi per voglia
blocks.translation: And, thinking that I did it from desire

blocks.source: di manicar, di sùbito levorsi
blocks.translation: Of eating, on a sudden they uprose,

blocks.source: e disser: “Padre, assai ci fia men doglia
blocks.translation: And said they: ‘Father, much less pain ’twill give us

blocks.source: se tu mangi di noi: tu ne vestisti
blocks.translation: If thou do eat of us; thyself didst clothe us

blocks.source: queste misere carni, e tu le spoglia”.
blocks.translation: With this poor flesh, and do thou strip it off.’

blocks.source: Queta’mi allor per non farli più tristi;
blocks.translation: I calmed me then, not to make them more sad.

blocks.source: lo dì e l’altro stemmo tutti muti;
blocks.translation: That day we all were silent, and the next.

blocks.source: ahi dura terra, perché non t’apristi?
blocks.translation: Ah! obdurate earth, wherefore didst thou not open?

blocks.source: Poscia che fummo al quarto dì venuti,
blocks.translation: When we had come unto the fourth day, Gaddo

blocks.source: Gaddo mi si gittò disteso a’ piedi,
blocks.translation: Threw himself down outstretched before my feet,

blocks.source: dicendo: “Padre mio, ché non m’aiuti?”.
blocks.translation: Saying, ‘My father, why dost thou not help me?’

blocks.source: Quivi morì; e come tu mi vedi,
blocks.translation: And there he died; and, as thou seest me,

blocks.source: vid’ io cascar li tre ad uno ad uno
blocks.translation: I saw the three fall, one by one, between

blocks.source: tra ’l quinto dì e ’l sesto; ond’ io mi diedi,
blocks.translation: The fifth day and the sixth; whence I betook me,

blocks.source: già cieco, a brancolar sovra ciascuno,
blocks.translation: Already blind, to groping over each,

blocks.source: e due dì li chiamai, poi che fur morti.
blocks.translation: And two days called them after they were dead;

blocks.source: Poscia, più che ’l dolor, poté ’l digiuno».
blocks.translation: Then fasting proved more powerful than grief.”

blocks.source: Quand’ ebbe detto ciò, con li occhi torti
blocks.translation: When he had said this, with his eyes distorted,

blocks.source: riprese ’l teschio misero co’ denti,
blocks.translation: The wretched skull resumed he with his teeth,

blocks.source: che furo a l’osso, come d’un can, forti.
blocks.translation: Which, as a dog’s, upon the bone were strong.

blocks.source: Ahi Pisa, vituperio de le genti
blocks.translation: Ah! Pisa, thou opprobrium of the people

blocks.source: del bel paese là dove ’l sì suona,
blocks.translation: Of the fair land there where the ‘Si’ doth sound,

blocks.source: poi che i vicini a te punir son lenti,
blocks.translation: Since slow to punish thee thy neighbours are,

blocks.source: muovasi la Capraia e la Gorgona,
blocks.translation: Let the Capraia and Gorgona move,

blocks.source: e faccian siepe ad Arno in su la foce,
blocks.translation: And make a hedge across the mouth of Arno

blocks.source: sì ch’elli annieghi in te ogne persona!
blocks.translation: That every person in thee it may drown!

blocks.source: Che se ’l conte Ugolino aveva voce
blocks.translation: For if Count Ugolino had the fame

blocks.source: d’aver tradita te de le castella,
blocks.translation: Of having in thy castles thee betrayed,

blocks.source: non dovei tu i figliuoi porre a tal croce.
blocks.translation: Thou shouldst not on such cross have put his sons.

blocks.source: Innocenti facea l’età novella,
blocks.translation: Guiltless of any crime, thou modern Thebes!

blocks.source: novella Tebe, Uguiccione e ’l Brigata
blocks.translation: Their youth made Uguccione and Brigata,

blocks.source: e li altri due che ’l canto suso appella.
blocks.translation: And the other two my song doth name above!

blocks.source: Noi passammo oltre, là ’ve la gelata
blocks.translation: We passed still farther onward, where the ice

blocks.source: ruvidamente un’altra gente fascia,
blocks.translation: Another people ruggedly enswathes,

blocks.source: non volta in giù, ma tutta riversata.
blocks.translation: Not downward turned, but all of them reversed.

blocks.source: Lo pianto stesso lì pianger non lascia,
blocks.translation: Weeping itself there does not let them weep,

blocks.source: e ’l duol che truova in su li occhi rintoppo,
blocks.translation: And grief that finds a barrier in the eyes

blocks.source: si volge in entro a far crescer l’ambascia;
blocks.translation: Turns itself inward to increase the anguish;

blocks.source: ché le lagrime prime fanno groppo,
blocks.translation: Because the earliest tears a cluster form,

blocks.source: e sì come visiere di cristallo,
blocks.translation: And, in the manner of a crystal visor,

blocks.source: rïempion sotto ’l ciglio tutto il coppo.
blocks.translation: Fill all the cup beneath the eyebrow full.

blocks.source: E avvegna che, sì come d’un callo,
blocks.translation: And notwithstanding that, as in a callus,

blocks.source: per la freddura ciascun sentimento
blocks.translation: Because of cold all sensibility

blocks.source: cessato avesse del mio viso stallo,
blocks.translation: Its station had abandoned in my face,

blocks.source: già mi parea sentire alquanto vento;
blocks.translation: Still it appeared to me I felt some wind;

blocks.source: per ch’io: «Maestro mio, questo chi move?
blocks.translation: Whence I: “My Master, who sets this in motion?

blocks.source: non è qua giù ogne vapore spento?».
blocks.translation: Is not below here every vapour quenched?”

blocks.source: Ond’ elli a me: «Avaccio sarai dove
blocks.translation: Whence he to me: “Full soon shalt thou be where

blocks.source: di ciò ti farà l’occhio la risposta,
blocks.translation: Thine eye shall answer make to thee of this,

blocks.source: veggendo la cagion che ’l fiato piove».
blocks.translation: Seeing the cause which raineth down the blast.”

blocks.source: E un de’ tristi de la fredda crosta
blocks.translation: And one of the wretches of the frozen crust

blocks.source: gridò a noi: «O anime crudeli
blocks.translation: Cried out to us: “O souls so merciless

blocks.source: tanto che data v’è l’ultima posta,
blocks.translation: That the last post is given unto you,

blocks.source: levatemi dal viso i duri veli,
blocks.translation: Lift from mine eyes the rigid veils, that I

blocks.source: sì ch’ïo sfoghi ’l duol che ’l cor m’impregna,
blocks.translation: May vent the sorrow which impregns my heart

blocks.source: un poco, pria che ’l pianto si raggeli».
blocks.translation: A little, e’er the weeping recongeal.”

blocks.source: Per ch’io a lui: «Se vuo’ ch’i’ ti sovvegna,
blocks.translation: Whence I to him: “If thou wouldst have me help thee

blocks.source: dimmi chi se’, e s’io non ti disbrigo,
blocks.translation: Say who thou wast; and if I free thee not,

blocks.source: al fondo de la ghiaccia ir mi convegna».
blocks.translation: May I go to the bottom of the ice.”

blocks.source: Rispuose adunque: «I’ son frate Alberigo;
blocks.translation: Then he replied: “I am Friar Alberigo;

blocks.source: i’ son quel da le frutta del mal orto,
blocks.translation: He am I of the fruit of the bad garden,

blocks.source: che qui riprendo dattero per figo».
blocks.translation: Who here a date am getting for my fig.”

blocks.source: «Oh», diss’ io lui, «or se’ tu ancor morto?».
blocks.translation: “O,” said I to him, “now art thou, too, dead?”

blocks.source: Ed elli a me: «Come ’l mio corpo stea
blocks.translation: And he to me: “How may my body fare

blocks.source: nel mondo sù, nulla scïenza porto.
blocks.translation: Up in the world, no knowledge I possess.

blocks.source: Cotal vantaggio ha questa Tolomea,
blocks.translation: Such an advantage has this Ptolomaea,

blocks.source: che spesse volte l’anima ci cade
blocks.translation: That oftentimes the soul descendeth here

blocks.source: innanzi ch’Atropòs mossa le dea.
blocks.translation: Before Atropos has set it loose.

blocks.source: E perché tu più volentier mi rade
blocks.translation: And, that thou mayest more willingly remove

blocks.source: le ’nvetrïate lagrime dal volto,
blocks.translation: From off my countenance these glassy tears,

blocks.source: sappie che, tosto che l’anima trade
blocks.translation: Know that as soon as any soul betrays

blocks.source: come fec’ ïo, il corpo suo l’è tolto
blocks.translation: As I have done, his body by a demon

blocks.source: da un demonio, che poscia il governa
blocks.translation: Is taken from him, who thereafter rules it,

blocks.source: mentre che ’l tempo suo tutto sia vòlto.
blocks.translation: Until his time has wholly been revolved.

blocks.source: Ella ruina in sì fatta cisterna;
blocks.translation: Itself down rushes into such a cistern;

blocks.source: e forse pare ancor lo corpo suso
blocks.translation: And still perchance above appears the body

blocks.source: de l’ombra che di qua dietro mi verna.
blocks.translation: Of yonder shade, that winters here behind me.

blocks.source: Tu ’l dei saper, se tu vien pur mo giuso:
blocks.translation: This thou shouldst know, if thou hast just come down;

blocks.source: elli è ser Branca Doria, e son più anni
blocks.translation: It is Ser Branca d’ Oria, and many years

blocks.source: poscia passati ch’el fu sì racchiuso».
blocks.translation: Have passed away since he was thus locked up.”

blocks.source: «Io credo», diss’ io lui, «che tu m’inganni;
blocks.translation: “I think,” said I to him, “thou dost deceive me;

blocks.source: ché Branca Doria non morì unquanche,
blocks.translation: For Branca d’ Oria is not dead as yet,

blocks.source: e mangia e bee e dorme e veste panni».
blocks.translation: And eats, and drinks, and sleeps, and puts on clothes.”

blocks.source: «Nel fosso sù», diss’ el, «de’ Malebranche,
blocks.translation: “In moat above,” said he, “of Malebranche,

blocks.source: là dove bolle la tenace pece,
blocks.translation: There where is boiling the tenacious pitch,

blocks.source: non era ancora giunto Michel Zanche,
blocks.translation: As yet had Michel Zanche not arrived,

blocks.source: che questi lasciò il diavolo in sua vece
blocks.translation: When this one left a devil in his stead

blocks.source: nel corpo suo, ed un suo prossimano
blocks.translation: Within his body, and likewise a near kinsman

blocks.source: che ’l tradimento insieme con lui fece.
blocks.translation: Who had committed that betrayal with him.

blocks.source: Ma distendi oggimai in qua la mano;
blocks.translation: But hitherward stretch out thy hand forthwith,

blocks.source: aprimi li occhi». E io non gliel’ apersi;
blocks.translation: Open mine eyes;”—and open them I did not,

blocks.source: e cortesia fu lui esser villano.
blocks.translation: And to be rude to him was courtesy.

blocks.source: Ahi Genovesi, uomini diversi
blocks.translation: Ah, Genoese! ye men at variance

blocks.source: d’ogne costume e pien d’ogne magagna,
blocks.translation: With every virtue, full of every vice

blocks.source: perché non siete voi del mondo spersi?
blocks.translation: Wherefore are ye not scattered from the world?

blocks.source: Ché col peggiore spirto di Romagna
blocks.translation: For with the vilest spirit of Romagna

blocks.source: trovai di voi un tal, che per sua opra
blocks.translation: I found of you one such, who for his deeds

blocks.source: in anima in Cocito già si bagna,
blocks.translation: In soul already in Cocytus bathes,

blocks.source: e in corpo par vivo ancor di sopra.
blocks.translation: And still above in body seems alive!
